top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on a simple, general mechanism: at the magic wavelength the lattice shifts both clock levels equally, so thousands of neutral atoms are interrogated without light-shift error, combining ensemble statistics with the small systematics of a trapped ion. The systematics are understood quantitatively and the 1e-18 performance is reproduced independently at JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST and SYRTE across species. The two-name allocation (Katori for the concept and first demonstration, Ye for record accuracy and many-body clocks) is clean and not a misattribution of the central idea, and the citation can be worded to distinguish it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system prizes. P002 is a strong, distinct discovery, but its credit leaves a visible theory gap (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang; 3D work) and rests on one group for the first observation, so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no collaboration with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp, and only same-region (Gothenburg/Chalmers) proximity to colleagues Johansson and Olsson.
